title: SDK First-Run Starter Kit and Runtime Stubs
author: Dylan Park
body:
Overview

This guide provides a compact, opinionated starter kit to get a new Redwood SDK integration running locally in under 20 minutes. It pairs a lightweight sample app, runtime stubs for embedding/generation calls, and a troubleshooting matrix of canonical fixes our support team uses most frequently. The goal is a reproducible first-run experience for frontend and backend engineers who are onboarding to Redwood’s hosted and dedicated inference flows.

Who this is for
- Engineers building production integrations with Redwood (frontend, backend, platform)
- SDK maintainers who need a minimal, testable harness to exercise API patterns
- Support engineers triaging early-stage integration issues

What you get with this starter kit
- A minimal sample app (Node + Python examples) that calls Redwood generation and embeddings APIs
- Local runtime stubs that mock network and streaming behavior for deterministic development
- A recommended config file and developer-telemetry hook for fast observability alignment
- A short canonical-fixes table for top-first-run support issues

Prerequisites
1. Git and Docker installed (Docker only required for full local runtime emulation)
2. Node 18+ and Python 3.10+ installed for examples
3. Redwood API key (test key) provisioned in the developer sandbox
4. 300 MB free disk for local caches and logs

Quickstart (20-minute path)
1) Clone the starter kit\   git clone git@internal.redwood.dev:dx/sdk-first-run-starter-kit.git && cd sdk-first-run-starter-kit

2) Environment: copy the example env and set a test key\   cp example.env .env\   # Open .env and set REDWOOD_API_KEY and DEV_MODE=local-stub

3) Start the local stub server (Node)\   cd stubs && npm install && npm run start

4) Run the sample Node app (generation quick path)\   cd ../samples/node && npm install && npm run start

5) Inspect the local telemetry page\   open http://localhost:8082/telemetry (shows requests, latencies, token counts)

Local runtime stubs (what they emulate)
- Auth and API surface: returns deterministic request IDs and enforces per-route quota headers
- Streaming: splits text output into chunks with configurable delays to emulate network jitter\- KV cache behavior: a simple LRU with TTL that mirrors the platform default (60s)
- Error injection endpoints: /stubs/inject to reproduce 429/503/faults for client resilience tests

File layout (short)
- stubs/ : Node-based runtime stubs and fault injector\- samples/node/ : Express + minimal client demonstrating streaming + fallback\- samples/python/ : FastAPI sample showing embeddings -> rerank flow\- config/dev-config.yaml : recommended default dev settings (caching, batch limits)

Recommended dev-config.yaml (annotated)
- max_batch_tokens: 2048  # keep small locally to exercise batching logic\- streaming_chunk_ms: 60  # smaller than prod to surface chunk handling\- prefix_cache_ttl_s: 60  # mirrors platform default

Note: the file above is included as config/dev-config.yaml within the starter kit.

Sample usage examples
Node (generation, streaming fallback):
```
// samples/node/index.js (excerpt)
const { RedwoodClient } = require('redwood-sdk');
const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, baseUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_BASE || 'http://localhost:8081' });

async function run() {
  try {
    const stream = await c.generateStream({ model: 'gpt-lite-1', prompt: 'Summarize the release notes' });
    for await (const chunk of stream) {
      process.stdout.write(chunk.text);
    }
  } catch (e) {
    // fallback to synchronous short-call
    const res = await c.generate({ model: 'gpt-lite-1', prompt: 'Summarize the release notes', max_tokens: 120 });
    console.log(res.text);
  }
}
run();
```

Python (embeddings -> similarity):
```
# samples/python/embeddings_demo.py (excerpt)
from redwood_sdk import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'], base_url=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_BASE','http://localhost:8081'))

items = ['doc A text', 'doc B text']
embs = c.embed_batch(items)
q = c.embed('query text')
# simple cosine loop
scores = [(i, cosine(q, e)) for i, e in enumerate(embs)]
print(sorted(scores, key=lambda s: s[1], reverse=True))
```

Developer telemetry and observability (recommended hooks)
- Export per-request token counts and model latency as tags: request_id, route, model_variant, token_input, token_output, upstream_latency_ms\- Sampled traces (1%) cross service: client -> stub -> remote (or hosted)\- Local telemetry UI exposes recent requests, error classification, and histogram of per-token latency

Canonical fixes (top-first-run support issues)
1) Symptom: App never receives streaming chunks (only final result after long delay)\   Root cause: Developer started the stub server with STREAMING_DISABLED=true or used an older SDK that defaulted to long-polling\   Fix: Restart stubs with STREAMING_ENABLED=true; upgrade SDK to 2.4.1+ (see /samples/node/package.json)\   Verify: Streaming chunks appear within 100ms of first token generation in telemetry page

2) Symptom: 429 responses when exercising batch endpoints locally\   Root cause: local stub uses a conservative per-second quota by default (Q=5/s) to simulate production throttles\   Fix: Update config/dev-config.yaml -> local_quota_per_s: 50 for stress testing or use the inject endpoint to bypass throttles: POST /stubs/inject {"type":"quota_bypass"}\   Verify: Batch calls succeed without 429s and telemetry shows sustained throughput

3) Symptom: Embeddings mismatch vs. hosted sandbox (vector distances different)\   Root cause: Developer accidentally used the stubbed embedding model (emb-stub-v1) rather than the sandbox model (emb-ssd-2)\   Fix: In .env set REDWOOD_MODEL_EMBEDDING=emb-ssd-2 and restart app. Run the provided golden-run script: ./tools/golden_compare.sh\   Verify: Distance variance falls below 3% on the golden corpus

4) Symptom: SDK throws certificate errors in corporate networks\   Root cause: TLS interception / custom CA not present in Node/Python trust stores\   Fix: Add the corporate root CA to the runtime trust store or set REDWOOD_TLS_TRUST_FILE to the CA bundle path for local dev (documented in example.env)\   Verify: HTTPS calls succeed; telemetry shows 200 responses for health-checks

Runbook: Turning a local prototype into a dedicated test harness
1. Replace stubs with a staging endpoint: set REDWOOD_BASE=https://staging-inference.redwood.internal and keep credentials segregated.
2. Pin a model variant: set MODEL_OVERRIDE to the exact model hash used in your QA to avoid surprise rollouts.
3. Run the smoke test suite (./tools/smoke.sh) which checks: connectivity, streaming, batch retry, and embedding stability.
4. Add a short Canary: route 1% of test traffic through the staging endpoint with tracing enabled for a day.

Maintenance notes
- Refresh the sample model names quarterly with the platform catalog; add integration tests to CI to start stubs automatically.
- Archive old golden corpora annually to keep the starter kit lightweight.

Appendix: Useful commands
- Start local stubs: cd stubs && npm run start\- Run Node sample: cd samples/node && npm run start\- Run Python sample: cd samples/python && python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt && python app.py\n
If you hit unexpected behavior, file a ticket in #dx-support with the stub trace ID from the telemetry page and the output of ./tools/collect-dev-logs.sh.
